label: Lipoma
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts

- Most common benign soft tissue tumor in adults
- Usually subcutaneous, < 5 cm, but can be larger; deep (intramuscular/retroperitoneal) forms require exclusion of ALT/WDLS  
- Composed of mature, uniform adipocytes without atypia or lipoblasts
- Deep/large (>10 cm) or retroperitoneal tumors require exclusion of MDM2 and CDK4 amplification to rule out atypical lipomatous tumor/well-differentiated liposarcoma [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html) [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
- Recurrence is rare and related to incomplete excision or deep location

## Terminology

- Definition: Benign tumor composed of mature adipocytes, essentially identical to normal fat [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html)
- Subtypes (not synonyms): Intramuscular lipoma, chondrolipoma [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html)
- No recommended synonyms; “fetal lipoma” and others are not recommended for pediatric variants

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria

- **Essential:**
  - Proliferation of mature, uniform adipocytes without atypia or lipoblasts [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html) [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
  - Absence of nuclear atypia or hyperchromasia
  - Fibrous septa may be present but are paucicellular
  - For retroperitoneal, deep, or large (>10 cm) tumors: negativity for both MDM2 and CDK4 by IHC/FISH is required to exclude ALT/WDLS [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
- **Desirable:**
  - Intramuscular variant shows entrapment or admixing of skeletal muscle fibers
  - Heterologous elements (benign cartilage or bone) in specific subtypes (chondrolipoma, osteolipoma)
  - Structural rearrangement of chromosome 12q13-15, especially involving HMGA2 gene [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
  - S-100 positivity in adipocytes supportive but not required

## Etiology/Pathogenesis

- Associated with rearrangements of chromosome 12q13-q15 (HMGA2 gene) [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
- Less commonly, rearrangement of 6p21 (HMGA1 gene) [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
- Pathophysiology includes reactivated expression of HMGA2 protein
- Negative for MDM2 and CDK4 amplification (ALT/WDLS positive for these markers)

## Clinical Issues

- **Epidemiology:**
  - Most common mesenchymal tumor in adults  
  - Slight male predominance
  - Most common between ages 40–60 [BST Horvai](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/_asset_library/textbooks/BST_Horvai/page_images/BST_Horvai_page_0298.png)
  - Multifocal in ~5%; may be seen in Cowden and Bannayan-Riley-Ruvalcaba syndromes [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
- **Sites:**
  - Most frequent: superficial subcutaneous tissue of upper back, proximal extremities, abdominal wall [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html)
  - Deep sites: intramuscular (esp. thigh), parosteal, visceral (GI tract, bronchial tree, oral cavity)
- **Presentation:**
  - Usually painless, mobile, slow-growing subcutaneous mass
  - May have specific symptoms when in GI, bronchus, or other unusual locations
- **Natural History:**
  - Uniformly benign course; no risk of metastasis  
- **Treatment:**
  - Simple excision is curative [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
  - Recurrence <5%, mainly with incomplete excision or if intramuscular/deep-seated

## Macroscopic

- Well-circumscribed, sometimes thinly encapsulated, homogeneous yellow, fatty mass [BST Horvai](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/_asset_library/textbooks/BST_Horvai/page_images/BST_Horvai_page_0298.png)
- Superficial lipomas: usually <5 cm, mobile [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
- Intramuscular/deeper lesions: often larger, may entrap or surround structures
- Osteolipoma/chondrolipoma: contain visible foci of bone/cartilage

## Microscopic

- Uniform proliferation of mature adipocytes with small, eccentric nuclei; sheets or lobules of bland fat cells
- Paucicellular fibrous septa may be present
- No nuclear atypia, mitoses, or lipoblasts
- Intramuscular type: mature adipocytes infiltrate and entrap skeletal muscle fibers, sometimes with atrophic muscle
- Fat necrosis and scattered foamy macrophages occasionally seen, especially in larger or traumatized tumors
- Heterologous elements: benign cartilage (chondrolipoma) or bone (osteolipoma) may form nodules

![Lipoma: homogeneous sheets of mature adipocytes](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_PICS/BST/5372.jpg)
![Intramuscular lipoma: skeletal muscle fibers surrounded by adipocytes](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_PICS/BST/5373.jpg)
![Osteolipoma: nodule of metaplastic bone/cartilage](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_PICS/BST/5375.jpg)
![Uniform adipocytes with small, eccentric nuclei](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/bst_horvai/bst_horvai_p0299_fig04_fig_3.jpeg)
![Intramuscular lipoma with admixed skeletal muscle](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/bst_horvai/bst_horvai_p0299_fig01_fig_4.jpeg)

## Cytology

- Smears/FNA show mature adipocytes with a single large lipid droplet
- Nuclei are small and inconspicuous [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
- No cytologic atypia or lipoblasts present

## Ancillary Tests

- **Immunohistochemistry:**
  - S-100 positive in adipocytes (supportive but not specific) [BST Horvai](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/_asset_library/textbooks/BST_Horvai/page_images/BST_Horvai_page_0298.png)
  - Rb retained in conventional lipoma (lost in spindle cell and pleomorphic types) [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
  - MDM2, CDK4, and p16 negative (positivity would suggest ALT/WDLS) [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
- **Molecular / Genetics:**
  - HMGA2 gene rearrangements or 12q13-15 aberrations in many lipomas [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
  - No MDM2 or CDK4 amplification [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html) [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
- **Molecular testing is not required for routine cases; mandatory to exclude MDM2 and CDK4 amplification in deep/large (>10 cm) or retroperitoneal tumors**

## Radiology

- **Ultrasound:** Variably echogenic or isoechoic, well-defined mass [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
- **MRI:** Isointense to subcutaneous fat on all sequences; discrete, encapsulated mass [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
- **CT:** Discrete, encapsulated fat-density mass [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
![Isointense mass on MRI](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/softtissueadiposelipomaradRenne1.png)
![Discrete encapsulated mass on CT](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/softtissueadiposelipomaradRenne2.png)

## Differential Diagnosis

*Differential diagnoses depend on tumor subtype (conventional vs. spindle cell/pleomorphic, age, site) and are organized as primary (common/morphologic) and rare (special-site/cytologic mimics):*

- **Atypical Lipomatous Tumor / Well-Differentiated Liposarcoma (ALT/WDLS)**
  - Typically >10 cm, deep or retroperitoneal location (but superficial/classic lipomas can be large—critical is setting and molecular profile)
  - May show scattered atypical stromal cells and rare lipoblasts
  - MDM2/CDK4 amplification by IHC or FISH positive in ALT/WDLS, negative in conventional lipomas [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
- **Spindle Cell / Pleomorphic Lipoma**
  - Bland spindle cells and ropy collagen, variable fat; floret-type giant cells in pleomorphic variant
  - CD34 positive, Rb1 IHC loss; posterior neck/upper back of men [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposepleomorphicgeneral.html)
  - Overlaps with myofibroblastoma and desmoid-type fibromatosis [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html)
- **Angiolipoma**
  - Mature fat plus numerous small vessels, may contain fibrin thrombi
  - Often painful, most common in young adults’ forearms [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposeangiolipoma.html)
- **Lipoblastoma (pediatric)**
  - Lobulated, immature adipocytes/lipoblasts, myxoid stroma, prominent plexiform vasculature
  - Occurs almost exclusively in children <3 yrs [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoblastoma.html)
- **Hibernoma**
  - Multivacuolated brown fat cells with granular cytoplasm, central nuclei
  - Most common in adults, proximal thigh [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposehibernoma.html)
- **Myolipoma**
  - Composed of smooth muscle and mature fat; actin/desmin positive [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposemyolipoma.html)
- **Lipofibromatosis (pediatric)**
  - Mature adipose tissue with infiltrative fibroblasts; usually in hands/feet of infants [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissuelipofibromatosis.html)
- **Chondroid lipoma**
  - Mixture of fat and chondroid-appearing matrix
- **Fat-forming (lipomatous) solitary fibrous tumor**
  - Collagenous stroma, staghorn vessels, CD34+, STAT6+
- **Myofibroblastoma and Desmoid-type Fibromatosis**
  - Spindle cell lesions that can mimic spindle cell lipoma—distinguishable by morphology and IHC; myofibroblastoma often CD34+, desmoid-type fibromatosis with β-catenin positivity [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html)
- **Silicon Granuloma**
  - Foreign body giant cell response, may be confused with variably vacuolated adipocytic lesions [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html)
- **Neoplasms with clear cell morphology (rare)**
  - May resemble fat cytologically:
    - Signet-ring cell carcinoma
    - Balloon cell melanoma
    - Perivascular epithelioid cell tumor (PEComa)
  - Distinguished by clinical, immunophenotypic, and cytologic features [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html)

## Prognostic Factors

- Main cause of recurrence is incomplete excision (<5%) [BST Horvai](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/_asset_library/textbooks/BST_Horvai/page_images/BST_Horvai_page_0298.png)
- Deep/intramuscular and larger tumors more likely to recur if excision is incomplete
- No risk of metastasis

## Illustrative Cases

- 37-year-old woman with giant infiltrative lipoma of face; mimicked malignancy due to size and location [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)
- 58-year-old and 63-year-old women with intramuscular lipomas of the pectoralis major simulating breast mass
- Well-circumscribed intramuscular tumor of sternocleidomastoid muscle presenting as neck mass

cards.title: Lipoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Lipoma Section: localization Lipomas are most common in the upper back, proximal extremity, and abdominal region, and the majority present as a superficial (subcutaneous) soft tissue mass. A smaller subset are deep-seated, arising within skeletal muscle (intramuscular lipoma), on the surface of bone (parosteal lipoma), or within the tendon sheath, or they may involve the gastrointestinal tract, oral cavity, or bronchial tree. Intramuscular lipomas most frequently involve the thigh (40–50%), followed by the shoulder, chest wall, and upper limb. Rare examples of retroperitoneal lipomas with cytogenetic and molecular confirmation have also been reported. Synovial lipomatosis (lipoma arborescens) is a lipomatous proliferation of subsynovial connective tissue often associated with chronic joint disease, and recent work has shown that this adipocytic proliferation lacks HMGA2 overexpression, supporting a non-neoplastic reactive process.

cards.title: Lipoma — Differential diagnosis
cards.excerpt:
Angiolipoma:
Typically composed of two elements: mature adipocytes and branching capillary sized vessels, which often contain fibrin thrombi
Relative proportions of adipocytes and vessels varies and some lesions are almost completely composed of vascular channels

cards.title: Spindle cell / pleomorphic lipoma — Epidemiology
cards.excerpt:
Commonly affects middle aged to elderly men (45 - 70 years) (Cancer 1975;36:1852)
Very rare in patients < 20 years
< 10% of cases occur in women
Uncommon compared with conventional lipoma (ratio = 1:60)

cards.title: Spindle cell / pleomorphic lipoma — Sites
cards.excerpt:
Mostly superficial, extremely rare in deep soft tissue
80% arise in the subcutaneous tissue of the posterior neck, back and shoulders (Cancer 1975;36:1852, Cancer 1981;47:126)
20% involve different sites, including face, oral cavity and trunk / extremities (Acta Pathol Microbiol Scand A 1976;84:477, Histopathology 1987;11:803, Histopathology 2015;66:430, Am J Clin Pathol 2016;146:487)
Cases in women more likely to arise in atypical locations (Am J Surg Pathol 2017;41:1267)
Intramuscular and dermal based lesions rarely seen (Am J Clin Pathol 2016;146:487, Am J Dermatopathol 2000;22:496)

cards.title: Spindle cell / pleomorphic lipoma — Pathophysiology
cards.excerpt:
Characterized by partial or whole chromosome 13 or 16 deletions (Histopathology 1997;31:222)
Breakpoints cluster around 13q14 where the RB1 gene resides (Int J Cancer 2003;103:616)
Part of the so called 13q / RB1 family of tumors, which includes myofibroblastoma and cellular angiofibroma (Hum Pathol 2012;43:1887, Am J Surg Pathol 2016;40:3617, Mod Pathol 2011;24:82)

cards.title: Spindle cell / pleomorphic lipoma — Myxoid background with mast cells frequent
cards.excerpt:
Short and stubby spindle cells show occasional palisading
Rare lipoblasts present in half of cases (Hum Pathol 2017;65:140)
Infiltrative growth, necrosis, atypical spindle cells, pleomorphic lipoblasts and significant mitotic activity usually absent (Semin Diagn Pathol 2019;36:105)
Fat poor and fat free subtype: contains little (< 5%) to no fat (Am J Dermatopathol 2007;29:437, Am J Dermatopathol 2009;31:423)
Myxoid subtype: contains abundant myxoid stroma (Pathol Int 2014;64:346)
(Pseudo) angiomatous subtype: contains dilated endothelial lined channels and nodules of floating tumor (Histopathology 1994;24:565, Pathol Int 2007;57:26)
Plexiform variant has been described (Histopathology 1995;27:533)
Focal cartilaginous and osseous metaplasia rarely present (Histopathology 1987;11:803)
Extramedullary hematopoiesis may occur (Histopathology 2001;39:215)
Microscopic (histologic) imagesContributed by Laura Warmke, M.D., Jeanne Meis, M.D. and AFIP

cards.title: Spindle cell / pleomorphic lipoma — Soft tissue, back, excision
cards.excerpt:
Spindle cell lipoma (see comment)
Comment: Sections show a benign adipocytic neoplasm with bland spindle cells and eosinophilic collagen bundles in a myxoid background with scattered mast cells. No necrosis, marked cytologic atypia or significant mitotic activity is identified. Immunohistochemical stains show that the spindle cells are diffusely positive for CD34, while demonstrating loss of RB1. These results support the above diagnosis.

cards.title: Chondroid lipoma — Pathophysiology
cards.excerpt:
Shows recurrent t(11;16)(q13;p13) translocation with resultant C11orf95 and MRTFB fusion (Genes Chromosomes Cancer 2010;49:810)
Megakaryoblastic leukemia 2 (MKL2) / myocardin related transcription factor B (MRTFB) acts as coactivator of transcription factor serum response factor (SRF)
SRF controls cellular processes including cytoskeleton organization, cell migration, growth and differentiation

Requires presence of classic histologic features (i.e., presence of lipoblasts, chondroid cells and adipocytes in a myxohyaline matrix in a circumscribed lobulated tumor)
Diagnosis can also be made on cytology (Am J Surg Pathol 1999;23:1300)

cards.title: Chondroid lipoma — Radiology description
cards.excerpt:
CT typically shows a well defined, heterogeneously enhancing mass with variable areas of fat attenuation
Can exhibit calcification and ossification on radiographs (Australas Med J 2012;5:355, Skeletal Radiol 2004;33:670)
MRI usually shows a well defined mass with lobulated areas of T2 hyperintense or fluid-like signal intensity (Balkan Med J 2015;32:107, Skeletal Radiol 1996;25:592)
Appears isointense or hypointense to muscle, with focal hyperintense areas (fat areas) on T1 weighted MR images

missing_essentials: Ancillary: Negativity for CDK4 or p16 not specified clearly in Essential Criteria (only MDM2, but evidence requires negativity for both MDM2 and CDK4 for exclusion of ALT/WDLS).

Atypical Lipomatous Tumor/Well-differentiated Liposarcoma defined: Size >10 cm, deep/retroperitoneal location highlighted, but should be clearer that even superficial/classic lipoma can be large, though the critical risk is deep location with molecular evidence of MDM2/CDK4.
Differential: No mention of myofibroblastoma and desmoid-type fibromatosis, which are spindle cell lipoma lookalikes per evidence.
Differential: No mention of fat-forming (lipomatous) solitary fibrous tumor, which is an explicit ddx in WHO.
Differential: No mention of silicon granuloma and clear cell-rich tumors (signet-ring cell carcinoma, balloon cell melanoma, PEComa), all listed as rare in DDx by WHO.
Differential: Spindle cell/pleomorphic lipoma can overlap with myofibroblastoma and desmoid-type fibromatosis—should be stated to reflect WHO.
redundant: Spindle cell/pleomorphic lipoma information is repeated in both Key Facts and Microscopic/Variants/Differential.
confusing: Prognostic Factors: The statement 'No risk of metastasis' appears both under Clinical Issues/Natural History and here—not always problematic, but could be consolidated.

Differential Diagnosis section is not clearly organized by importance (main pitfalls vs. rare lookalikes) and does not reflect that DDx varies by subtype and location (per WHO and PathOutlines distinctions).

Restructure and clarify the differential section to reflect primary and rare mimics, including mention that the DDx varies by subtype/location.
